title: Finisguerra 2015 · sound motion and corticospinal excitability
citation: Finisguerra, A., Canzoneri, E., Serino, A., Pozzo, T., & Bassolino, M. (2015). Moving sounds within the peripersonal space modulate the motor system. Neuropsychologia, 70, 421–428.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

schedule.comparators: Separate silent PRE and POST TMS blocks, then touch-cued sound-location check.

published_method.response: No voluntary motor response on sound–TMS trials. Give a speeded verbal report for rare right-hand electrical touch trials. Normalize the right first dorsal interosseous peak-to-peak MEP against pooled silent pre/post baseline.

stimulus_type.value: Apparent moving sound in approaching and receding directions

source_provenance.value: Eight hidden serial speakers, custom microcontroller and MATLAB
source_provenance.gap: Original sound files and playback code are unavailable.

trajectory_path.source: Finisguerra et al. (2015), §2.3.1 and original publisher Fig. 1a
trajectory_path.gap: The caption gives 15 cm arm-to-first-source separation. The two unlabeled end speakers and the six 15–90 cm nominal probes do not establish an absolute 3D coordinate origin or exact channel-switch schedule.

gain_envelope.value: Microcontroller varies volume across serial speakers, with a 70 dB maximum at the closest position for both directions.
gain_envelope.gap: Original envelope shape, speaker switch times and calibration reference details are unknown.

value.driver: Custom MATLAB, microcontroller volume sequencing, and CED-triggered TMS
value.calibration: Phonometer before each experimental block. Maximum 70 dB at the near position in both directions.
value.unknown: Signal identity, transfer law, channel gains, software versions, loudspeaker models, meter weighting, microphone position and room geometry.

renderer_or_apparatus.gap: Signal identity, transfer law, channel gains, software versions, loudspeaker models, meter weighting, microphone position and room geometry.

value: moving sound + rare tactile target without TMS
trial_rows_families.source: Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §2.3.1 and Fig. 1 and Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §§2.3.1, 3.2

condition_intermixing.value: Rare touch trials randomized among direction × distance TMS trials. Silent baselines separate.
condition_intermixing.source: Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §2.3.1 and Fig. 1 and Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §§2.3.1, 3.2

blocked_or_random_order.value: PRE → four experimental blocks → POST, then localization. Main directions and distances randomized.
blocked_or_random_order.source: Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §2.3.1 and Fig. 1 and Neuropsychologia p. 424, §§2.3.2, 3.1
blocked_or_random_order.gap: The authors distribute TMS trials equally across four blocks. Per-block catch counts are unreported.

iti_jitter_policy.gap: The described interval is software-controlled. Selection distribution and interval anchor are unknown. The paper gives the touch-to-TMS gap as at least 4–5 s.

response_window.gap: Speeded verbal detection applies to rare touch. No exact deadline or capture latency.

value: establish FDI hotspot and resting motor threshold
task_sequence_rules.source: Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §2.3.1 and Fig. 1 and Neuropsychologia p. 424, §§2.3.2, 3.1

value.gap: Current, pulse width, waveform and intensity selection method are unreported.

tactile_stimulus.gap: Current, pulse width, waveform and intensity selection method are unreported.

soa_table.gap: The TMS delay uses the time the sound reaches a position. Exact offsets from audio onset and numerical peripheral tactile SOAs are unknown.

baseline_strategy.value: 100 × mean experimental peak-to-peak MEP / mean pooled PRE and POST MEP.

baseline_timing.value: Silent PRE and POST resting TMS blocks bookend the main experiment.

catch_trial_type.value: Occasional right-hand electrical cue with speeded verbal detection and no TMS

baseline_count.gap: Paper describes 12 trials measuring excitability and two trials with touch and no TMS in each block. Inclusion of those two in the stated 12 is unclear.

block_count.source: Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §2.3.1 and Fig. 1 and Neuropsychologia pp. 422–424, §§2.3.1, 3.2

total_trial_count.gap: Main experimental session only. Baselines, calibration and post-task localization are separate.

implementation_gaps: The eight-speaker crossfades, waveforms, precise position trigger timestamps and original controller code are unavailable.

Reproduction requires synchronized qualified TMS/EMG, calibrated auditory and electrical delivery, a documented routing for the vocal attention check, and safe laboratory handling. A tactile SOA cannot stand in for the TMS trigger.
The paper’s wording does not establish the touch onset relative to the sound. Keep those attention trials distinct from the published 50 ms post-position TMS timing.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
